minutes.headline: Capital Planning heard the last of five department presentations; no project votes, with ranking meetings set for Dec 4, 18 and 21.
minutes.summary: The committee heard the facilities director and the Parks Commission chair present proposed capital projects, including locks and key cards, public safety building design, the DPW roof and floor, asbestos testing at TCP, Ritter flooring, senior center parking, Marshall Pond weeds, McNeil Park design and a basketball court. Members questioned lumped design and construction requests and spending on buildings whose future is undecided. Only adjournment was voted; the meeting ended by setting tentative dates for discussion, ranking and a final list.

public_comment.topic: A speaker corrected last meeting's information: school bus drivers do not need a CDL, though some state certification is required; suggested talking to neighbouring districts.
Asked about the cost of school swing set replacement; told the equipment is a six-digit figure in a future year and engineering is planned this year alongside driveway and parking.
Asked on behalf of neighbours whether street tree maintenance could be a capital item or citizens could petition; told it is an operating item with a DPW line and a tree warden.

budget_items.topic: MSBA planning numbers (assessment/schematic design and windows)
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said the accelerated repair program requirements may affect the windows planning number; the assessment and schematic design number seemed safe.
Facilities director said the full list for the year is just over a million dollars.

budget_items.topic: Public safety building second floor design
budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted design money would be followed by a six-figure construction request and further records work.
A member found the estimate high for the small roof; it is based on a cost per square foot and could come in lower.
Member confirmed the coating would be touched up rather than fully reapplied.
An estimate for full asbestos testing was given but the figure was unclear in the captions.
Members questioned spending on flooring that may be replaced if the building is reorganized.

budget_items.topic: Senior center parking design and construction
budget_items.what_was_said: A member objected to lumping design and construction in one request.
The scope was proposed to shrink from the whole pond to a front section; a revised figure was requested in writing.
The request is for survey and conceptual design work.
Parks asked to move it into the coming year; members asked about cost and life of the surface.

decisions.decision: The facilities director will send the updated project spreadsheet to the committee and the town manager, with a single notes column on scope.
Tentative meeting dates: Monday Dec 4 at 7 p.m. pending room, Monday Dec 18 and Thursday Dec 21 at 6 p.m.
Plan: discussion Dec 4, individual rankings compiled and discussed Dec 18, final list Dec 21.
Parks asked that the basketball court project be treated as part of the coming fiscal year; the facilities director agreed to add it.

what_happened.line: Capital Planning heard the last of five department presentations and took no project votes; only adjournment was voted.
Tentative dates were set: discussion Dec 4, individual rankings compiled and discussed Dec 18, and a final list Dec 21.
The facilities director and the Parks chair presented requests, among them locks and key cards, public safety building design, DPW roof and floor, Ritter flooring and senior center parking.
Members questioned requests that lump design with construction, and spending on flooring in a building whose future is undecided.
The facilities director will send an updated project spreadsheet with a notes column on scope, and will add the basketball court to the coming fiscal year's list.

why_it_matters: These meetings shape the list of building and park projects that may later reach town meeting, so questions about design-only requests, repairs to buildings with uncertain futures, and scope changes affect which projects residents are asked to fund.
watch_next: Ranking meetings on Dec 4 (time pending room), Dec 18 and Dec 21, ending in a final project list.
The updated project spreadsheet from the facilities director, and a revised written figure for Marshall Pond weed treatment.
